title: AI修正後、採用していい？ 保存・再起動・既存機能を確かめる受入票
snippet: AIから「修正完了、テストも合格」と報告された。けれど、その版を普段使いに移してよいかは、まだ判断できない。 既存のGUI・デスクトップアプリでは、変更した画面だけでなく、保存後・再起動後に状態が残ること、変更禁止だった機能が動くことも確かめたいところです。 この記事では、修正依頼の書き方ではなく、 完成報告を受け取った後に、人間が実機で採否を決めるための受入票 を作ります。以下の手順は確認方法の提案であり、登場するアプリや結果は説明用の架空例です。 1．操作する前に「何を確かめるか」を固定する 続きをみる

title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training
snippet: arXiv:2611.31427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents operate through harnesses that define system prompts, action formats, feedback loops, and resource constraints. A model may possess the knowledge needed to solve a task yet fail to express that knowledge through a particular harness. This raises a basic question: when a policy fails under a given harness, is it missing task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface? We distinguish two components of agentic competence: task competence, the knowledge and reasoning needed to solve a task, and interface competence, the ability to act on that knowledge through a given harness. Across four reasoning and agentic benchmarks, we show that harness-conditioned training yields vastly different outcomes depending on how these interact. title: ContextLure: Exploiting Benign Conversation History for Indirect Prompt Injection
snippet: arXiv:2611.31424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLMs become more capable, agents can perform more complex tasks with tools and maintain longer interactions with users. These benign conversations contain evidence on task results, user concerns, and operational constraints. The risk is that attackers who can observe benign conversations (evidence) may construct stronger indirect prompt injections without increasing the attackers' control over prior turns or the later injection. However, we still lack a clear study of how effectively attackers can select and use this evidence. To address this gap, we introduce ContextLure, a red-teaming framework in which an attacker silently observes an existing benign conversation, extracts evidence, and constructs an injection. title: Antares-Smaug: Adversarial Names, Tokens and Attack Rewrites: Sanitisers Miss Unseen Generalisations
snippet: arXiv:2611.31347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laya is an open decision model: given a text, a question and K named options with descriptions, it returns one probability per option in a single pass, and software may act on the answer unseen. We attack six Laya models with 81 programmatic edits of 566 synthetic items (injected sentences, label leaks, edited descriptions, decoy options, invisible and look-alike characters, floods) and report the share of correctly answered items hijacked or lost, with bootstrap intervals. Attack wordings that no defence was built from win the attacker's option on 59% of items for released Laya and 36% for fine-tune v1 (trained on 109 written injections). An injection works through the option name: a sentence naming an option steers the released model even when negated (32%), while an imperative naming no option does not (5%). title: What People Choose Not to Say: A Multimodal Benchmark for Fine-Grained Information Manipulation in Conversations
snippet: arXiv:2611.31346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in MLLMs have improved social understanding, enabling models to recognize emotions and distinguish truthful from deceptive behaviors. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on coarse-grained emotion recognition or binary truth-deception detection, overlooking the diverse ways people manipulate information in conversations, such as withholding, leakage, fabrication, evasion, and defensive counterclaim. Understanding these behaviors requires reasoning about underlying facts, participant knowledge, and conversational context, making them difficult to evaluate reliably. To address this gap, we introduce InfoCon, a multimodal benchmark for fine-grained information manipulation in conversations. InfoCon identifies six fine-grained strategies and derives a coarse consistency label from their factual and interactional relations.

title: Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Sets for Incomplete Data
snippet: arXiv:2611.31329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attribute reduction in incomplete information systems is difficult because missing values break the equivalence-class structure of rough set theory. We propose the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set (COFRS) model. Each object is described by its set of present attributes. The similarity of two objects is a weighted overlap on the attributes present in both, divided by the fixed number of attributes |A| instead of the size of their union, so missing values are penalised globally and are not matched as wildcards. From this similarity we define a soft dependency degree based on weighted granule consistency, and we search for reducts by greedy backward elimination in O(|U|^2 |A|^2) time. title: App Storeの審査で「Guideline 4.3」と言われたら。最初に直す3つのチェックリスト
snippet: 結論：Guideline 4.3は「スパム」の条項です。落ちたらコードを書き直す前に、却下理由の原文を読んで「(a)か(b)か、4.2の併記か」を切り分けてください。直すポイントは3つだけです。 App Storeにアプリを出すと、ときどき「Guideline 4.3 - Spam」という理由で却下されます。40本ほど作ってきた中で、審査でつまずく原因の大半はバグではなく「ガイドラインの読み違い」でした。4.3はスパム対策の条項で、Appleの言い分はシンプルです。「同じようなアプリを量産しないでほしい」「すでにあるものと見分けがつかないものは要らない」。公式のガイドライン原文に沿って、最初に直す3つを整理します。 続きをみる
